vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: mapbox-mcp-devkit-patterns
Version: 1.0.1

The skill bundle provides legitimate integration patterns and documentation for the Mapbox MCP DevKit Server. It contains standard setup instructions, tool descriptions (e.g., style and token management), and workflow examples across files like SKILL.md, AGENTS.md, and various reference documents. No evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or harmful prompt injection was found; all external links point to official Mapbox resources (mapbox.com and github.com/mapbox).

llm.summary: The skill's instructions, files, and requirements are internally consistent with a Mapbox MCP DevKit integration guide; nothing indicates it is trying to do something other than document and recommend DevKit workflows, though there are a few practical risks users should watch for (credentials in configs, npx usage, committing project configs).

dimensions.detail: The name/description (Mapbox MCP DevKit integration patterns) matches the content: guidance on styles, tokens, validation, and MCP configuration. Required artifacts (none) align with an instruction-only pattern library — nothing requests unrelated system or cloud credentials.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and references describe exactly the expected operations (creating/listing styles and tokens, validating GeoJSON, editing MCP config for various assistants). They ask the AI or user to write style JSON to files and to edit local agent config files — reasonable for a dev workflow but grants the agent permission to read/write project files and to modify MCP config. The docs also suggest committing project-level MCP config; that could inadvertently expose secrets if not handled carefully.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec or code to download. The only potentially noteworthy instruction is to use npx (e.g., 'npx mcp-remote ...') or clone the upstream GitHub repo to self-host the DevKit server — both are normal for developer tooling but mean code may be executed from npm or GitHub at user discretion.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not declare or require environment variables, but it documents use of MAPBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN for self-hosted setups and recommends storing tokens in environment variables. This is appropriate for the purpose, but examples also show project-level configs and env entries that could be accidentally committed — a practical risk of credential leakage rather than an incoherence in purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and does not request persistent privileges. It instructs how to configure MCP servers for local AI assistants (editing per-user or per-project config), which is expected for this integration and limited to user-level configuration changes.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is a documentation/pattern pack for Mapbox DevKit and appears coherent with that purpose. Before installing or following examples: 1) Never commit access tokens or env files to source control — remove MAPBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN or any secrets from project-level configs before committing. 2) When using the hosted URL (https://mcp-devkit.mapbox.com/mcp), confirm you trust the operator of that endpoint and prefer OAuth flows over embedding tokens. 3) Using npx runs code from the npm registry — only run npx commands you trust. 4) If self-hosting, keep access tokens out of committed config and restrict who can read your dev machine configs. If you want deeper assurance, provide the actual MCP server URL you plan to use and whether you expect the AI to write files or modify local agent configs — that would let me flag any further risks.
